elements.quote: The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.

elements.quote: The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.

elements.quote: Relevant randomised controlled trials were selected, their risk of bias assessed, and the data then extracted and analysed.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates that relevant randomized controlled trials were selected (inclusion of RCTs) but does not specify detailed main inclusion and exclusion criteria (e.g. age limits, excluded study types) in the abstract.

elements.quote: A search was performed on the 22nd of July 2020 to identify articles comparing surgical fixation versus clinical management for flail chest in adults, with a description of the outcome parameters ...
elements.reason: The abstract reports the date the search was performed (22nd of July 2020) but does not list the information sources/databases searched in the abstract.

elements.quote: Relevant randomised controlled trials were selected, their risk of bias assessed, and the data then extracted and analysed.
elements.reason: The abstract states that risk of bias was assessed but does not specify the method or tool used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: Relevant randomised controlled trials were selected, their risk of bias assessed, and the data then extracted and analysed.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates that data were extracted and analysed and reports pooled results, but it does not specify the methods used to present and synthesize results (e.g. meta-analysis model, summary measures) in detail.

elements.quote: 157 patients were included from four studies in the analyses, with 79 and 78 patients in the surgical and non-surgical groups, respectively.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies and participants and gives group counts, summarizing key study/sample characteristics.

elements.quote: The pooled effects of all outcomes tended towards favouring surgical intervention. Surgical intervention was associated with lower rates of pneumonia ( I 2 = 46%, Tau 2 = 0.16, p = 0.16), significantly lower rates of tracheostomy ( I 2 = 76%, Tau 2 = 0.67, p = 0.02), and a significantly lower duration of mechanical ventilation ( I 2 = 88%, Tau 2 = 33.7, p < 0.01) in comparison to the non-surgical management methods.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for main outcomes and heterogeneity statistics, but does not provide the number of studies or participants contributing to each specific outcome or exact effect size estimates with confidence intervals for each outcome.

elements.quote: The pooled effects of all outcomes tended towards favouring surgical intervention. ... (I 2 = 46%, Tau 2 = 0.16, p = 0.16) ... (I 2 = 76%, Tau 2 = 0.67, p = 0.02) ... (I 2 = 88%, Tau 2 = 33.7, p < 0.01)
elements.reason: Although meta-analytic heterogeneity statistics are reported, the abstract does not report the summary effect estimates (e.g. risk ratios, mean differences) nor their confidence or credible intervals.

elements.quote: The pooled effects of all outcomes tended towards favouring surgical intervention. Surgical intervention was associated with lower rates of pneumonia ... significantly lower rates of tracheostomy ... and a significantly lower duration of mechanical ventilation ... in comparison to the non-surgical management methods.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and states that outcomes favored the surgical group.

elements.quote: There is a need for further well-designed studies with sufficient sample sizes to confirm the results of this study and also detect other possible effects of surgical intervention in the treatment of traumatic flail chest in adults.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly notes uncertainty and the need for further studies (imprecision/limited evidence) but does not explicitly summarize specific limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision.

elements.quote: Our results suggest that surgical intervention reduces the need for tracheostomy, reduces the time spent in the intensive care unit following a traumatic flail chest injury and could reduce the risk of acquiring pneumonia after such an event.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their potential implications for practice.

elements.quote: Funding No funding was received for this study.
elements.reason: The funding statement is present in the main text (Potential Biases In The Review Process) but the abstract itself does not specify the primary source of funding; the checklist asks for this information in the abstract.
No register name or registration number for the review is provided in the abstract or other retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Although the number of patients included in the analyses was small (157 patients), surgery appeared to be beneficial for the main outcome, length of stay in ICU, and also for the secondary outcomes, pneumonia, tracheostomy and length of stay on mechanical ventilation. Considerable heterogeneity was detected for the duration of mechanical ventilation and tracheostomy outcomes to warrant caution when interpreting the results. It is possible that these results are down to chance.
elements.reason: Explicitly describes current state of knowledge (small number of patients, observed benefits) and important uncertainties (considerable heterogeneity, possible chance findings).

elements.quote: There is a need for further well-designed studies with sufficient sample sizes to confirm the results of this study and also detect other possible effects of surgical intervention in the treatment of traumatic flail chest in adults.
elements.reason: Direct statement explaining the importance and need for conducting the review and for further well-designed larger studies to confirm findings.

elements.quote: The results of this systematic review are by and large consistent with the results seen in the previous retrospective studies and meta-analyses [22-24]. However, previous studies [23-25] only included three of the RCTs and reported on 61 patients whilst this study includes 4 RCTs with 157 patients in total. Hence, our study is more conclusive than these previous studies due to the larger number of patients involved in surgical fixation.
elements.reason: Explicitly cites and compares previous reviews/studies, explains how the current review differs (includes an additional RCT and more patients) and thus justifies the need for the present review.
No text in the provided evidence describes a proposed mechanism of action for the surgical intervention (why or how surgical fixation would lead to the observed outcomes).
No evidence provided of a logic model or any statement addressing hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: Purpose The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.
elements.reason: The review objective is explicitly stated (to compare safety and efficacy of surgical fixation versus non-surgical interventions in adults with flail chest), but it is not presented using a formal question‑formulation framework (e.g., explicit PICO framing).

elements.quote:
Purpose The objective of this systematic review is to compare the safety and efficacy of surgical fixation of rib fractures against non-surgical interventions for the treatment of flail chest in the adult population.

The primary outcome of this systematic review is the length of stay in the intensive care unit (ICU). The overall length of stay in hospital was also evaluated. The secondary outcomes of this review are the in-hospital mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation and complications such as the adverse effects of the intervention (bone infection, wound infection and pain), and the adverse progression in pulmonary status (tracheostomy and pneumonia).
elements.reason: For an intervention review, the planned comparison is explicitly stated (surgical fixation versus non-surgical/clinical management in adults with flail chest) and key outcome measures are listed, providing P (adult flail chest patients), I (surgical fixation), C (non-surgical/clinical management), and O (ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, mortality, ventilation duration, complications).

elements.quote: Studies were only included if they meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) prospective RCTs, (2) comparing surgical treatment against non-surgical, clinical management of flail chest injury. ... Studies that included any non-flail or nontraumatic rib fractures were excluded. Any studies including individuals aged < 18 years were also excluded. Letters, conference papers, reviews, abstracts and case reports were excluded, along with any observational studies.
elements.reason: The text explicitly lists study characteristics used for eligibility (prospective RCTs, comparison surgical vs non-surgical), excluded populations (non-flail fractures, age <18), and excluded study designs (letters, conference papers, observational studies).

elements.quote: To minimise retrieval and publication bias, no limitations were set with regard to language, publication date or publication status. ... Letters, conference papers, reviews, abstracts and case reports were excluded, along with any observational studies.
elements.reason: The review states explicit report characteristic eligibility (no limitations on language, publication date or status) and also lists excluded publication types.

elements.quote: Studies were excluded if no results were available.
elements.reason: The manuscript states studies with 'no results available' were excluded but does not distinguish whether exclusion was because outcomes were not measured versus outcomes were measured but not reported.

elements.quote: | Paper                | Outcomes                         | Surgical group      | Non-surgical group   | P value   |
elements.reason: Tables and text consistently present groups used in syntheses as 'Surgical group' versus 'Non-surgical group', matching the comparison defined in the inclusion criteria and used in the quantitative synthesis.

elements.quote: To minimise retrieval and publication bias, no limitations were set with regard to language, publication date or publication status.
elements.reason: A rationale is provided explaining why no restrictions were placed on language/publication date/status. However, no explicit rationale is given for other notable restrictions (e.g. restricting to prospective RCTs, excluding observational studies or excluding participants aged <18), so rationale reporting is incomplete.

Forced vital capacity, forced expiratory volume one (FEV1) and results from a quality-of-life questionnaire (Rand 36 health survey) were evaluated at 3- and 6-months post-discharge. This study was also interested in how many participants were still using narcotics for pain control two weeks post-discharge.
elements.reason: Some outcomes have specified measurement time points (e.g., 2 weeks, 3 and 6 months, 6 and 12 months), but time frames are not provided comprehensively for every outcome domain listed.
The report does not state whether all results compatible with each outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought across studies.
There is no description of a process used to select among multiple compatible results when not all were sought (no selection rules reported).
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance, nor rationales for any such changes, are reported in the provided evidence.
No changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains, nor rationales, are reported in the evidence.

elements.quote: Studies were only included if they meet the following inclusion criteria: (1) prospective RCTs, (2) comparing surgical treatment against non-surgical, clinical management of flail chest injury. ... Fig. 1 Prisma flow chart illustrating the literature search process ... The four studies (see Supplementary Table 2 for full characteristics of the studies) were prospective RCTs and involved 157 patients [11-14].
elements.reason: The manuscript provides clear inclusion and exclusion criteria for selecting studies and a PRISMA flow chart showing which studies progressed to qualitative and quantitative synthesis; however, it does not explicitly describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each specific synthesis (for example, how study intervention characteristics were tabulated and compared against planned groups for each synthesis). Thus the requirement is only partially met.

No retrieved evidence describes methods used to prepare collected data for presentation or synthesis (for example, handling missing summary statistics, imputations, or data conversions). The Statistical Analysis section (chunk_id text_5) only reports software, heterogeneity metrics, and that forest plots were used, but does not describe any data-preparation or conversion methods.

elements.quote: The analysis has been carried out in R version 3.6.2 using the 'meta' package version 4.13.
elements.reason: The software (R), version (3.6.2) and package ('meta' v4.13) used for statistical synthesis are explicitly reported.
A meta-analysis was performed (see text_5), so describing an alternative synthesis because meta-analysis was not possible does not apply.

elements.quote: Between-study heterogeneity assessed by the I 2 value, along with an estimate of the between-study variance in a randomeffects meta-analysis, ­ Tau 2 .
elements.reason: The authors state a random-effects meta-analysis was used (model reported), but they do not provide a rationale for choosing the random-effects model.

elements.quote: The analysis has been carried out in R version 3.6.2 using the 'meta' package version 4.13. Graphically, data were presented as forest plots.
elements.reason: The statistical software and package are reported and forest plots are mentioned, but the specific statistical pooling method/metrics (e.g. effect measure, weighting method) are not described.

elements.quote: Between-study heterogeneity assessed by the I 2 value, along with an estimate of the between-study variance in a randomeffects meta-analysis, ­ Tau 2 .

The evidence does not identify any planned syntheses judged impossible/inappropriate nor provides reasons; no such plans are reported.

The manuscript reports statistical heterogeneity metrics (I2 and Tau2) (see text_5) but does not specify any methods used to explore possible causes of heterogeneity such as subgroup analyses or meta-regression.
No description is provided of any subgroup analyses or meta-regression factors, factor levels, or expected directions of effect modification in the retrieved evidence.
The report does not state whether any heterogeneity analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both; only I2 and Tau2 are reported (text_5).
There is no information about methods used to compare subgroup effects (no subgroup analyses or comparison methods are described in the provided evidence).
When meta-analysis was unsuitable, no informal methods for exploring heterogeneity (including factors and levels) are described in the retrieved text.
The manuscript does not identify any heterogeneity analyses as pre-specified or post-hoc; no such analyses are described in the available evidence.

No text in the provided evidence describes any sensitivity analyses or gives details of sensitivity analyses performed. The Statistical Analysis section (chunk_id: text_5) describes heterogeneity measures and software but does not mention sensitivity analyses.
No text in the provided evidence identifies any sensitivity analyses, pre-specified or not. There is no statement indicating that any sensitivity analyses were conducted or whether any were post-hoc.

elements.quote: The results of this systematic review are by and large consistent with the results seen in the previous retrospective studies and meta-analyses [22-24]. However, previous studies [23-25] only included three of the RCTs and reported on 61 patients whilst this study includes 4 RCTs with 157 patients in total. Hence, our study is more conclusive than these previous studies due to the larger number of patients involved in surgical fixation. Even so, more well-designed multi-centred RCTs are needed to produce strong evidence that could influence clinical practice.
